dedupe_keys.name: msha mine data retrieval system and open government data sets

description: The Mine Safety and Health Administration publishes data on every mine under its jurisdiction in the United States through two channels: the Mine Data Retrieval System, an interactive lookup by mine, and the Open Government data sets, bulk pipe-delimited files updated every Friday afternoon. The data sets, filed by operators and inspectors under 30 CFR Part 50 and MSHA enforcement, cover mines and their status, controller and operator history, quarterly and yearly employment and coal production by subunit (underground, surface, open pit, preparation plant), accidents, injuries and illnesses from 2000 onward, inspections, violations, assessed penalties, civil penalty dockets, coal dust and metal and non-metal area samples. Each file has a definition file. Coverage is national, per mine identifier, with records from 1 January 2000. Access is free without registration; as U.S. Government works the files are in the public domain. Caveats read on 26 September 2026: the retrieval system was reported down and its PDF and Excel export as faulty, the weekly update was postponed, metal and non-metal operators do not report production, and maintenance runs each Friday night. For simulation the data give a mine asset inventory with operating status, historical accident and incident records, and production time series for supply-chain, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related catalogue records include the USGS Mineral Resources Data System, which covers deposits and mines worldwide.
